equity_bridge.note: ~8.5x NCI share of adjusted EBITDA (~$200M/yr; Q2-26 earnings release 'Adjusted EBITDA attributable to noncontrolling interests' $52M). Book NCI $1,197M at 30-Jun-2026 (XBRL MinorityInterest).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: nominal mid-cycle growth (terminal 2.0%). Every trailing CAGR is a cycle-phase artifact: 3-yr windows start at the 2022 crack-spread peak, 5-yr windows start at the 2020 COVID trough (FY2020 EPS -9.06 and owner FCF -936 make the 5-yr EPS/FCF CAGRs undefined). Revenue 10-yr CAGR of 3.0% (FY2015-25) is the least distorted series and supports ~2-2.5% nominal.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR +7.0% vs EPS 3-yr -22.6% and revenue 5-yr +15.6%: divergence far exceeds 30%. Cause is cyclicality plus portfolio change (DCP consolidation 2022-23, WRB 100% from Oct-2025, Coastal Bend 2025, European retail sale 2025), not a growth signal. Equity CAGR is not used.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR (-33.2%) is close to reported (-31.8%): SBC is ~0.15% of revenue and is not what drives the FCF series; the commodity cycle is. Owner FCF history 2018-25: 4,834 / 766 / -936 / 4,013 / 8,409 / 4,314 / 2,122 / 2,509; LTM Jun-26 6,174 (super-cycle).

scenario_narratives.base: The diesel super-cycle (~7mm bpd offline in Asia/Middle East plus ~1.4mm bpd Russia) persists through Q4-2026 and fades through H1-2027 as offline capacity returns; realized refining margins settle near the ~$12/bbl seen in Q3/Q4-2025 rather than the $24/bbl of Q2-2026, helped modestly by permanent closures (PSX Los Angeles, Valero Benicia). Midstream reaches the guided $4.5B EBITDA run-rate by YE2027 (Zeus gas plant, Coastal Bend fractionator), CPChem's Golden Triangle and Ras Laffan crackers start in 2027 into a still-soft chemicals cycle, Renewable Fuels hovers near breakeven as credit values normalise, and capex holds at ~$2.5B. Mid-cycle consolidated EBITDA ~$10.4B; the near-term windfall is captured once in years 1-2 and goes to deleveraging and buybacks, not into the terminal value.
scenario_narratives.bull: Structural rationalisation is real: global closures plus slow restarts lift the through-cycle realized refining margin to ~$15/bbl, the super-cycle runs to mid-2027, Midstream beats $4.5B with Permian volume growth, CPChem's new capacity lands into a chemicals upcycle, and SAF/LCFS credit values keep Rodeo profitable. Mid-cycle EBITDA ~$13B; this is roughly the sell-side ($300-335 PT) view of 2027 earnings power. Elliott-driven portfolio discipline continues without a value-destroying break-up.
scenario_narratives.bear: Offline Russian and Middle-East barrels plus new Indian/Middle-East/Chinese capacity return in early 2027 and cracks revert to 2024 levels (~$9/bbl realized; refining adjusted EBITDA ~$1.6B), Renewable Fuels slips back to losses as credits oversupply (it lost $380M in 2025), CPChem's new crackers start into a chemicals trough, and California/EU regulation keeps squeezing the legacy footprint. Midstream (~$4.2B) is the floor. Mid-cycle EBITDA ~$7.5B, and the >50%-of-OCF payout commitment collides with a capex programme that cannot be cut quickly.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Phillips 66 on mid-cycle owner FCF, not on the 2026 super-cycle print. The LTM Jun-26 owner FCF ($6.2B) and Q2-26's $5.9B adjusted EBITDA quarter are peak-cycle; the model captures the windfall once in years 1-2 and capitalises a ~$10.4B mid-cycle EBITDA (anchored on the first two post-WRB, post-LA quarters at ~$12/bbl realized margins plus guided Midstream and CPChem growth). The market price implies the super-cycle is close to permanent.
key_risks_to_valuation: Duration of the diesel super-cycle: each extra quarter at Q2-26 margins adds roughly $3B of EBITDA (~$5-6/share after tax)
Mid-cycle refining margin: each $1/bbl of realized margin is ~$0.75B of EBITDA per year (~760 MMbbl/yr processed), roughly $15-18/share capitalised
Midstream $4.5B run-rate execution and any Elliott-driven separation (a SOTP crystallisation would argue for a higher blended terminal multiple than 14x)
CPChem cash retention for Golden Triangle/Ras Laffan: equity earnings are assumed to equal distributions across the cycle

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 126.74-277.12
data_sources.financials: PSX_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL); SEC companyfacts API (D&A, cash taxes, interest paid, SBC, buybacks, NCI, equity-affiliate earnings, debt); 10-K FY2025 and FY2023/FY2020 capital-spending tables (capex is a custom psx: tag absent from companyfacts); Q2-2026 10-Q cover (shares) and balance sheet; Q4-2025 and Q2-2026 earnings releases (8-K Ex 99.1) for segment and consolidated EBITDA adjusted for special items and realized refining margins

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 399.02M common shares on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover plus ~2.0M incremental share-based-award shares (Q2-26 10-Q EPS note; diluted weighted average was 402.6M for Q2 while the count was still falling). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so buybacks are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $220M (XBRL); LTM proxy = FY2025. Equity-award withholding taxes are not separately disclosed on the cash-flow statement; SBC is ~0.15% of revenue so the omission is immaterial (<$0.5/share).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $1,207M; H1-2026 $648M ($379M in Q2). Repurchaser: the flat count is funded. $10B authorization increase July 2026.
inputs.fy0_basis_note: FY0 is the twelve months to 30-Jun-2026 (revenue FY25 132,376 - H1-25 63,753 + H1-26 83,544 = 152,167), because net debt is taken from the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet. Using FY2025 as FY0 with a June balance sheet would count H1-2026's ~$3.9B of free cash flow twice (once in year-1 flows, once in the lower net debt). Projection year 1 is therefore Jul-2026 to Jun-2027.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: LTM Jun-26: OCF 8,925 (FY25 4,962 - H1-25 1,032 + H1-26 4,995) less capital expenditures & investments 2,531 (FY25 2,233 - H1-25 1,010 + H1-26 1,308) = 6,394. Owner FCF 6,174 after SBC. This LTM sits ON the super-cycle (Q2-26 adjusted EBITDA $5.9B, realized refining margin $24.08/bbl) and is NOT the run-rate the projection compounds; the forward build is component-based on a mid-cycle margin.

owner_fcf_history.note: OCF - capital expenditures & investments (10-K capital spending tables: 2,639/3,873/2,920/1,860/2,194/2,418/1,859/2,233) - SBC. Levered (after interest paid ~$0.9B/yr). 2018-25 mean $3.25B on a smaller asset base (pre-DCP consolidation, pre-WRB 100%, pre-Coastal Bend).

inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build. Risk-free 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.15 -> cost of equity ~10.1%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (BBB+), after-tax ~4.0%; market-value weights ~87/13 (equity $106B, net debt $16.5B) -> ~9.3%, rounded to 9.0% because a growing ~40% of EBITDA is fee-based Midstream. Same WACC in all scenarios: cyclicality is charged in the scenario flows (mid-cycle normalisation + 25% bear weight), not as a WACC premium (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost (~$600M/yr cash in FY2025) is already an operating expense inside EBITDA, and operating lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases (principal ~$30M/yr) sit inside total_debt via LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations and are not deducted from flows. One treatment per lease class, no double count.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (pre-NCI). NCI (mainly third-party interests in consolidated Midstream entities; NCI adjusted EBITDA ~$200M/yr, $52M in Q2-26) is charged ONCE, in the equity bridge at ~$1.7B (~8.5x NCI EBITDA; book NCI $1,197M at 30-Jun-2026).
inputs.equity_affiliate_treatment: CPChem (50%) and other equity affiliates enter EBITDA as reported equity earnings (the company's consolidated 'EBITDA adjusted for special items' basis, NOT the 'Adjusted EBITDA' that grosses up affiliates' proportional D&A/interest/tax). Equity earnings are assumed ~= distributions across the cycle; CPChem is currently retaining cash to fund Golden Triangle and Ras Laffan (H1-26 undistributed $600M), which is the cost of the 2027 earnings step-up modelled from year 2. Cash tax is applied to EBIT including after-tax equity earnings, a small (~$0.2B/yr) conservative overcharge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with mid-cycle normalisation (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, cyclical' + owner-fcf-adaptations). First valuation of PSX; no memory entry. Phillips 66 is an operating company (refining, midstream, marketing, chemicals JV), not a bank/REIT/holdco, so owner-FCF is the right engine; the cyclical adaptation is that the LTM base sits at a refining super-cycle peak and is NOT extrapolated. Mid-cycle anchor: consolidated EBITDA adjusted for special items was $2.42B in Q3-25 and $2.40B in Q4-25 at realized refining margins of $12.15-12.48/bbl (the first quarters with WRB 100%-consolidated and LA idled), i.e. ~$9.6B annualised; adding the guided Midstream step to a $4.5B run-rate by YE2027 (+~$0.6B) and CPChem's 2027 Golden Triangle/Ras Laffan start-ups (+~$0.3-0.4B equity earnings) gives the ~$10.4B base mid-cycle EBITDA from year 3. Q1-26 ($1.07B, $10.11/bbl, Winter Storm Fern) and Q2-26 ($5.75B, $24.08/bbl super-cycle) bracket it. Year 1 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) carries the super-cycle tail (~$12.8B base), year 2 fades (~$10.6B). Revenue is price-driven; the revenue path falls from the inflated Q2-26 price level toward ~$136B and the margin path is set so revenue x margin hits these EBITDA dollars. Working capital is price-driven noise, modelled at zero over the cycle (wc_capture 0). Capex: 2026 budget $2.37B ($1.1B sustaining, $1.3B growth), 2027 target ~$2.5B total; held ~1.86% of revenue (~$2.5B) against D&A ~1.72% (~$2.3B run-rate, H1-26 $1,143M) so the asset base is maintained. Interest income not stripped (net debt company). Terminal: 14x cap (Gordon at 9%/2% = 14.6x), a blend of ~10x for refining/marketing FCF and ~17x for fee-based Midstream; reported as the binding bound in the JSON.

bear.narrative: Offline capacity returns in early 2027; margins revert to 2024-like ~$9/bbl; ~$7.5B mid-cycle EBITDA with Renewables loss-making again.

base.narrative: Year-1 EBITDA ~$12.8B (super-cycle Q3/Q4-26 then fading H1-27), ~$10.6B in year 2, ~$10.4B mid-cycle from year 3 growing with nominal revenue.

bull.narrative: Super-cycle runs through mid-2027 (~$15B year 1) and settles at a structurally higher ~$13B mid-cycle (~$15/bbl realized refining margin) after permanent closures.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the valuation date is at a refining-margin peak and mean reversion from such peaks has been the historical norm (2008, 2015, 2022-24); the bear is a return to 2024 conditions, not a solvency case. Base 50% as the evidence-weighted mid-cycle. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (structural margin floor, chemicals upcycle, credit-value support).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
